		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = cells[r][c];
				if (cell == null) {
					throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null.");
				}
				this.cells[r][c] = cell;
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
					Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(r, c);
					boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
					if (tc.isSource()) {
						if (isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell must not be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found.");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (!isInBounds(adjacent)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cell direction points outside the map.");
						}
						Cell adjacentCell = cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col];
						if (adjacentCell instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cell direction points into a wall at ("
									+ adjacent.row + "," + adjacent.col + ").");
						}
						foundSource = tc;
					} else {
						if (!isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found.");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (isInBounds(adjacent)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell direction must point outside the map.");
						}
						foundSink = tc;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found.");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found.");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell cell = cells[r][c];
		if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
			if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .
	 */
	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		if (!isInBounds(coord)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coordinate out of map bounds: " + coord);
		}
		Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at " + coord + " is not a FillableCell.");
		}
		cells[coord.row][coord.col] = new FillableCell(coord);
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0 || sourceCell == null) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer>> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.coord;
		queue.offer(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(start, 0));
		filledTiles.add(start);
		sourceCell.setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer> entry = queue.poll();
			Coordinate coord = entry.getKey();
			int dist = entry.getValue();
			if (dist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = coord.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isInBounds(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell cell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
					if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null) {
						fillableCell.setFilled();
						filledTiles.add(neighbor);
						queue.offer(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(neighbor, dist + 1));
					}
				} else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell terminationCell) {
					terminationCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.offer(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(neighbor, dist + 1));
				}
			}
		}
	}
}

The method `hasLost()` should return `true` if no new pipes were filled during the last round. The class `Map` tracks filled tiles in the `filledTiles` set and the count of previously filled tiles in `prevFilledTiles`. If after a round the number of filled tiles hasn't increased, it means no pipes were filled during that round, so the game is lost.

A correct implementation compares the current size of `filledTiles` with `prevFilledTiles`. If they are equal, return `true` (game lost), otherwise update `prevFilledTiles` and return `false`.

Here is the complete method:

```java
/**

	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}

			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {

			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3 in size.");
		}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		if (!isInBounds(coord)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coordinate out of map bounds: " + coord);
		}
		Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {

		filledTiles.remove(coord);

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0 || sourceCell == null) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer>> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.coord;
		queue.offer(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(start, 0));
		filledTiles.add(start);
		sourceCell.setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer> entry = queue.poll();
			Coordinate coord = entry.getKey();
			int dist = entry.getValue();
			if (dist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = coord.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isInBounds(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell cell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
					if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null) {
						fillableCell.setFilled();
						filledTiles.add(neighbor);
						queue.offer(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(neighbor, dist + 1));
					}
				} else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell terminationCell) {
					terminationCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.offer(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(neighbor, dist + 1));
				}
			}
		}
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		queue.offer(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isInBounds(neighbor) || visited.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (currentCell.isConnectedTo(neighborCell, dir)) {
					visited.add(neighbor);
					queue.offer(neighbor);
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	public void fillBeginTile() {
		sourceCell.setFilled();
	}

	@NotNull
	private List<Coordinate> getTraversedCoords() {
		return new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
	}

	public boolean hasLost() {

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3 in size.");
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
			}
		}
		for (int r = 1; r < rows - 1; r++) {
			for (int c = 1; c < cols - 1; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
		Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
		cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
		do {
			sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		} while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
		Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
		Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
		cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3 in size.");
		}
		if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array size mismatch.");
		}
		for (Cell[] row : cells) {
			if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array size mismatch.");
			}
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = cells[r][c];
				if (cell == null) {
					throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null.");
				}
				this.cells[r][c] = cell;
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
					Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(r, c);
					boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
					if (tc.isSource()) {
						if (isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell must not be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found.");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (!isInBounds(adjacent)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cell direction points outside the map.");
						}
						Cell adjacentCell = cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col];
						if (adjacentCell instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cell direction points into a wall at ("
									+ adjacent.row + "," + adjacent.col + ").");
						}
						foundSource = tc;
					} else {
						if (!isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found.");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (isInBounds(adjacent)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell direction must point outside the map.");
						}
						foundSink = tc;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found.");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found.");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell cell = cells[r][c];
		if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
			if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .
	 */
	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		if (!isInBounds(coord)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coordinate out of map bounds: " + coord);
		}
		Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at " + coord + " is not a FillableCell.");
		}
		cells[coord.row][coord.col] = new FillableCell(coord);
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0 || sourceCell == null) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer>> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.coord;
		queue.offer(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(start, 0));
		filledTiles.add(start);
		sourceCell.setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer> entry = queue.poll();
			Coordinate coord = entry.getKey();
			int dist = entry.getValue();
			if (dist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = coord.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isInBounds(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell cell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
					if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null) {
						fillableCell.setFilled();
						filledTiles.add(neighbor);
						queue.offer(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(neighbor, dist + 1));
					}
				} else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell terminationCell) {
					terminationCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.offer(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(neighbor, dist + 1));
				}
			}
		}
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		queue.offer(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isInBounds(neighbor) || visited.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (currentCell.isConnectedTo(neighborCell, dir)) {
					visited.add(neighbor);
					queue.offer(neighbor);
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

/**
 * <p>
 * Hint: The game is lost when a round ends and no pipes are filled during the round. Is

 * </p>
 *
 * @return {@code true} if the game is lost.
 */
public boolean hasLost() {
    if (filledTiles.size() == prevFilledTiles) {
        return true;
    }
    prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
    return false;
}

Response Text:---
The errors indicate that the constructors `Map(int, int)` and `Map(int, int, Cell[][])` are not recognized as constructors but rather as methods because they have a return type (`void`) or are declared incorrectly. In Java, constructors must not have a return type and must have the exact name of the class.

In your code, these two methods are declared as:

```java
public void Map(int rows, int cols) { ... }

public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) { ... }
```

This is invalid for constructors. They should be declared without any return type, like this:

```java
public Map(int rows, int cols) { ... }

public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) { ... }
```

Fixing this will resolve the compilation errors related to the constructors.

---

**Corrected class snippet with fixed constructors:**

```java
package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

    private final int rows;
    private final int cols;
    @NotNull
    final Cell[][] cells;

    private TerminationCell sourceCell;
    private TerminationCell sinkCell;

    @NotNull
    private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
    private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
    private Integer prevFilledDistance;

    // ... other methods unchanged ...

    /**
     * Constructs a map with given rows and cols.
     *
     * @param rows Number of rows.
     * @param cols Number of columns.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols) {
        if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3 in size.");
        }
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
                cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
            }
        }
        for (int r = 1; r < rows - 1; r++) {
            for (int c = 1; c < cols - 1; c++) {
                cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
            }
        }
        TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
        Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
        Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
        sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
        cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
        TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
        do {
            sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
        } while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
        Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
        Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
        sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
        cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
    }

    /**
     * Constructs a map with given rows, cols and cells.
     *
     * @param rows  Number of rows.
     * @param cols  Number of columns.
     * @param cells 2D array of cells.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
        if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3 in size.");
        }
        if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array size mismatch.");
        }
        for (Cell[] row : cells) {
            if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array size mismatch.");
            }
        }
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        TerminationCell foundSource = null;
        TerminationCell foundSink = null;
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
                Cell cell = cells[r][c];
                if (cell == null) {
                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null.");
                }
                this.cells[r][c] = cell;
                if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
                    Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(r, c);
                    boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
                    if (tc.isSource()) {
                        if (isEdge) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                                    "Source cell must not be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
                        }
                        if (foundSource != null) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found.");
                        }
                        Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
                        if (!isInBounds(adjacent)) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cell direction points outside the map.");
                        }
                        Cell adjacentCell = cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col];
                        if (adjacentCell instanceof Wall) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cell direction points into a wall at ("
                                    + adjacent.row + "," + adjacent.col + ").");
                        }
                        foundSource = tc;
                    } else {
                        if (!isEdge) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
                        }
                        if (foundSink != null) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found.");
                        }
                        Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
                        if (isInBounds(adjacent)) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell direction must point outside the map.");
                        }
                        foundSink = tc;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if (foundSource == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found.");
        }
        if (foundSink == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found.");
        }
        this.sourceCell = foundSource;
        this.sinkCell = foundSink;
    }

    // ... rest of the class unchanged ...
}

	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	public void fillBeginTile() {
		sourceCell.setFilled();
	}

	@NotNull
	private List<Coordinate> getTraversedCoords() {
		return new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
	}

		// TODO

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3 in size.");
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
			}
		}
		for (int r = 1; r < rows - 1; r++) {
			for (int c = 1; c < cols - 1; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
		Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
		cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
		do {
			sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		} while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
		Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
		Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
		cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3 in size.");
		}
		if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array size mismatch.");
		}
		for (Cell[] row : cells) {
			if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array size mismatch.");
			}
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = cells[r][c];
				if (cell == null) {
					throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null.");
				}
				this.cells[r][c] = cell;
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
					Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(r, c);
					boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
					if (tc.isSource()) {
						if (isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell must not be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found.");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (!isInBounds(adjacent)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cell direction points outside the map.");
						}
						Cell adjacentCell = cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col];
						if (adjacentCell instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cell direction points into a wall at ("
									+ adjacent.row + "," + adjacent.col + ").");
						}
						foundSource = tc;
					} else {
						if (!isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found.");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (isInBounds(adjacent)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell direction must point outside the map.");
						}
						foundSink = tc;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found.");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found.");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell cell = cells[r][c];
		if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
			if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .
	 */
	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		if (!isInBounds(coord)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coordinate out of map bounds: " + coord);
		}
		Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at " + coord + " is not a FillableCell.");
		}
		cells[coord.row][coord.col] = new FillableCell(coord);
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0 || sourceCell == null) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer>> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.coord;
		queue.offer(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(start, 0));
		filledTiles.add(start);
		sourceCell.setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer> entry = queue.poll();
			Coordinate coord = entry.getKey();
			int dist = entry.getValue();
			if (dist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = coord.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isInBounds(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell cell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
					if (fillableCell.getPipe() != null) {
						fillableCell.setFilled();
						filledTiles.add(neighbor);
						queue.offer(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(neighbor, dist + 1));
					}
				} else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell terminationCell) {
					terminationCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.offer(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(neighbor, dist + 1));
				}
			}
		}
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		queue.offer(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isInBounds(neighbor) || visited.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (currentCell.isConnectedTo(neighborCell, dir)) {
					visited.add(neighbor);
					queue.offer(neighbor);
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

Response Text:---
The errors indicate that the constructors `Map(int, int)` and `Map(int, int, Cell[][])` are not recognized as constructors because they are declared as `void` methods named `Map`, which makes them regular methods, not constructors. In Java, constructors must not have a return type, not even `void`.

**Fix:** Remove the `void` return type from these methods to properly define them as constructors.

Here is the corrected `Map` class constructors part with proper constructor declarations:

```java
/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

    private final int rows;
    private final int cols;
    @NotNull
    final Cell[][] cells;

    private TerminationCell sourceCell;
    private TerminationCell sinkCell;

    @NotNull
    private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
    private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
    private Integer prevFilledDistance;

    // ... other methods and fields ...

    // Correct constructor without return type
    public Map(int rows, int cols) {
        if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3 in size.");
        }
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
                cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
            }
        }
        for (int r = 1; r < rows - 1; r++) {
            for (int c = 1; c < cols - 1; c++) {
                cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
            }
        }
        TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
        Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
        Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
        sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
        cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
        TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
        do {
            sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
        } while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
        Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
        Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
        sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
        cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
    }

    // Correct constructor without return type
    public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
        if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3 in size.");
        }
        if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array size mismatch.");
        }
        for (Cell[] row : cells) {
            if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array size mismatch.");
            }
        }
        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
        TerminationCell foundSource = null;
        TerminationCell foundSink = null;
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
                Cell cell = cells[r][c];
                if (cell == null) {
                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null.");
                }
                this.cells[r][c] = cell;
                if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
                    Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(r, c);
                    boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
                    if (tc.isSource()) {
                        if (isEdge) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                                    "Source cell must not be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
                        }
                        if (foundSource != null) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found.");
                        }
                        Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
                        if (!isInBounds(adjacent)) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cell direction points outside the map.");
                        }
                        Cell adjacentCell = cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col];
                        if (adjacentCell instanceof Wall) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cell direction points into a wall at ("
                                    + adjacent.row + "," + adjacent.col + ").");
                        }
                        foundSource = tc;
                    } else {
                        if (!isEdge) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
                        }
                        if (foundSink != null) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found.");
                        }
                        Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
                        if (isInBounds(adjacent)) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell direction must point outside the map.");
                        }
                        foundSink = tc;
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        if (foundSource == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found.");
        }
        if (foundSink == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found.");
        }
        this.sourceCell = foundSource;
        this.sinkCell = foundSink;
    }

    // ... rest of the class ...
}
```

**Summary:**  
Change the two methods named `Map` from `public void Map(...)` to proper constructors `public Map(...)` by removing the `void` return type. This will fix the "constructor undefined" compilation errors.

            }

The error occurs because the constructor `Wall(Coordinate)` is defined as a method with a void return type (`public void Wall(Coordinate coord)`), which is not a constructor but a regular method. Constructors must not have a return type. To fix this, remove the `void` keyword so that the constructor is properly defined.

Here is the corrected `Wall` class with the proper constructor and the previously fixed `toSingleChar` method:

```java
package game.map.cells;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.PipePatterns;

/**
 * Represents a wall in {@link game.map.Map}.
 */
public class Wall extends Cell {

    /**
     * <p>
     * Hint: use {@link util.PipePatterns}
     * </p>
     *
     * @return the character representation of a wall in game
     */
    @Override
    public char toSingleChar() {
        return PipePatterns.WALL;
    }

    public Wall(Coordinate coord) {
        super(coord, PipePatterns.WALL);
    }
}
```

This will fix the "constructor undefined" compilation error and allow the tests to run successfully.

package game.map.cells;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.PipePatterns;

/**
 * Represents a wall in {@link game.map.Map}.
 */
public class Wall extends Cell {

    /**
     * <p>
     * Hint: use {@link util.PipePatterns}
     * </p>
     *
     * @return the character representation of a wall in game
     */
    @Override
    public char toSingleChar() {
        return PipePatterns.WALL;
    }

    public Wall(Coordinate coord) {
        super(coord, PipePatterns.WALL);
    }
}

Response Text:---
The error is caused by the fact that your Wall class has a method named `Wall` instead of a constructor. In Java, constructors must not have a return type, not even void. Your current code declares a method `public void Wall(Coordinate coord)` which is not a constructor, so the default constructor is missing and the call `new Wall(Coordinate)` fails.

To fix this, you need to replace the method `public void Wall(Coordinate coord)` with a proper constructor `public Wall(Coordinate coord)` (no return type).

Here is the corrected Wall class:

```java
package game.map.cells;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.PipePatterns;

/**
 * Represents a wall in {@link game.map.Map}.
 */
public class Wall extends Cell {

    /**
     * <p>
     * Hint: use {@link util.PipePatterns}
     * </p>
     *
     * @return the character representation of a wall in game
     */
    @Override
    public char toSingleChar() {
        return PipePatterns.WALL;
    }

    public Wall(Coordinate coord) {
        super(coord, PipePatterns.WALL);
    }
}
```

This change defines a proper constructor, which will resolve the "constructor Wall(Coordinate) is undefined" compilation error.

The `getConnections` method should return the directions in which this pipe connects based on its shape. Since the `Shape` enum represents different pipe shapes, each shape corresponds to a fixed set of connection directions (e.g., HORIZONTAL connects LEFT and RIGHT, VERTICAL connects UP and DOWN, etc.). If the shape is not recognized, the method should throw an `IllegalStateException`.

Here is a complete implementation of the `getConnections` method for the `Pipe` class:

```java
public Direction[] getConnections() {
    return switch (shape) {
        case HORIZONTAL -> new Direction[] {Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT};
        case VERTICAL -> new Direction[] {Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN};
        case TOP_LEFT -> new Direction[] {Direction.UP, Direction.LEFT};
        case TOP_RIGHT -> new Direction[] {Direction.UP, Direction.RIGHT};
        case BOTTOM_LEFT -> new Direction[] {Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT};
        case BOTTOM_RIGHT -> new Direction[] {Direction.DOWN, Direction.RIGHT};
        case CROSS -> new Direction[] {Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT};
        default -> throw new IllegalStateException("Unknown pipe shape: " + shape);
    };
}
```

Response Text:---
The method `createGame` initializes a JesonMor game by creating two players (user and computer), setting up a configuration with the given board size and move protection, placing initial pieces on the board, and returning a new JesonMor game instance. The user player is placed first in the player array and moves first, as required.

Here is a complete implementation of the `createGame` method that initializes the gameboard with two knights placed at positions (0,0) and (1,0) respectively, one for each player:

```java
public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    // Create the user player who moves first
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    // Create the computer player
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");
    // Create configuration with the two players, user player first
    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer }, numMovesProtection);
    // Create knights for each player
    Knight knight1 = new Knight(userPlayer);
    Knight knight2 = new Knight(computerPlayer);
    // Place the knights on the board at specified positions
    configuration.addInitialPiece(knight1, 0, 0);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(knight2, 1, 0);
    // Return a new JesonMor game initialized with this configuration
    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}
```

This method can be modified to add more pieces or different initial setups as needed by the assignment.

The assignment likely requires a more complete initial setup including Archers and possibly more Knights, placed according to the assignment's rules. The user player must be first and move first, which your code already does.

---

**Corrected `createGame` method:**

```java
public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    // Create players with user player first
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");

    // Create configuration with players and protection moves
    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer }, numMovesProtection);

    // Add initial pieces for user player (placed on bottom rows)
    // Example placement: Knights and Archers on first row (row size-1)
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(userPlayer), size - 1, 0);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(userPlayer), size - 1, 1);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(userPlayer), size - 1, 2);

    // Add initial pieces for computer player (placed on top rows)
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computerPlayer), 0, size - 1);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(computerPlayer), 0, size - 2);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computerPlayer), 0, size - 3);

    // Return the JesonMor game initialized with this configuration
    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}
```

---

- Added Archers as required by the test `testHalfArcher()`.  
- Added multiple pieces per player to avoid null pieces and satisfy board initialization tests.  
- Placed user player's pieces on the bottom row and computer player's pieces on the top row, assuming a standard board orientation.  
- Kept user player first in the player array to ensure they move first.

This should fix the test failures related to missing pieces and null references. Adjust piece positions if your assignment specifies different starting locations.

The test failures indicate that the initial board setup is incorrect:  
- `testHalfArcher()` expects exactly one Archer per player but found none.  
- `testPieceBelonging()` fails due to null pieces, meaning some board positions are empty where pieces are expected.  
- `testInitialBoard1()` expects no null pieces on initial positions.

The root cause is that pieces are not placed correctly according to the assignment's requirements. Usually, the board is square, and pieces should be placed on the first two rows for one player and the last two rows for the other, with the user player first and moving first.

**Fix:**  
- Place pieces on the first two rows for the computer player (top of the board).  
- Place pieces on the last two rows for the user player (bottom of the board).  
- Include both Knights and Archers, ensuring at least one Archer per player.  
- Fill the rows properly to avoid nulls.

Here is a corrected `createGame` method that places pieces accordingly:

```java
public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");
    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer }, numMovesProtection);

    // Place pieces for computer player on top two rows
    for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
        if (col % 2 == 0) {
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computerPlayer), 0, col);
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(computerPlayer), 1, col);
        } else {
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(computerPlayer), 0, col);
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computerPlayer), 1, col);
        }
    }

    // Place pieces for user player on bottom two rows
    int lastRow = size - 1;
    int secondLastRow = size - 2;
    for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
        if (col % 2 == 0) {
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(userPlayer), lastRow, col);
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(userPlayer), secondLastRow, col);
        } else {
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(userPlayer), lastRow, col);
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(userPlayer), secondLastRow, col);
        }
    }

    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}
```

This ensures:  
- Both players have Knights and Archers.  
- Pieces occupy the first two and last two rows fully, no nulls in these rows.  
- User player is first in the player array and moves first.  

This should fix the test failures.

Response Text:---
The `start` method should implement a game loop where players take turns in the order given by `configuration.getPlayers()`. For each turn:

- Set the current player.
- Get all available moves for the current player.
- Ask the player to choose the next move via `Player#nextMove(Game, Move[])`.
- Make the move by updating the board.
- Update the player's score.
- Refresh the output.
- Check if the move results in a winner by calling `getWinner`.
- If there is a winner, break the loop and return the winner.

Here is a complete implementation of the `start` method following these steps:

```java
@Override
public Player start() {
    // reset all things
    Player winner = null;
    this.numMoves = 0;
    this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    this.currentPlayer = null;
    this.refreshOutput();

    Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
    int playerCount = players.length;
    int turnIndex = 0;

    while (true) {
        this.currentPlayer = players[turnIndex];
        Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(this.currentPlayer);

        if (availableMoves.length == 0) {
            // No moves available for current player, skip turn or end game?
            // Here we just skip to next player
            turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
            continue;
        }

        Move chosenMove = this.currentPlayer.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
        movePiece(chosenMove);

        // Find the piece moved (piece at destination)
        Place dest = chosenMove.getDestination();
        Piece movedPiece = board[dest.x()][dest.y()];

        updateScore(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, chosenMove);
        this.numMoves++;
        this.refreshOutput();

        winner = getWinner(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, chosenMove);
        if (winner != null) {
            System.out.println();
            System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
            System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
            return winner;
        }

        turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
    }
}
```

This implementation respects the order of players, uses the provided methods to get moves, make moves, update scores, refresh output, and detect the winner. It loops indefinitely until a winner is found.

@Override
public Player start() {
    // reset all things
    Player winner = null;
    this.numMoves = 0;
    this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    this.currentPlayer = null;
    this.refreshOutput();

    Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
    int playerCount = players.length;
    int turnIndex = 0;

    while (true) {
        this.currentPlayer = players[turnIndex];
        Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(this.currentPlayer);

        if (availableMoves.length == 0) {
            // No moves available for current player, skip turn or end game?
            // Here we just skip to next player
            turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
            continue;
        }

        Move chosenMove = this.currentPlayer.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
        movePiece(chosenMove);

        // Find the piece moved (piece at destination)
        Place dest = chosenMove.getDestination();
        Piece movedPiece = board[dest.x()][dest.y()];

        updateScore(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, chosenMove);
        this.numMoves++;
        this.refreshOutput();

        winner = getWinner(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, chosenMove);
        if (winner != null) {
            System.out.println();
            System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
            System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
            return winner;
        }

        turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
    }

The `getWinner` method should determine if the last move made by `lastPlayer` results in a winning condition. Since the game is JesonMor (a variant of chess-like game), a typical winning condition might be capturing a specific piece (like a King) or meeting a certain score or board condition. However, from the provided code and context, the most straightforward way is to check if the last move captured an opponent's piece that causes the game to end or if the last player meets a winning condition.

Assuming the winning condition is that the last move captures a piece that ends the game (e.g., capturing a King or no opponent pieces left), or if the player reaches a certain score threshold (not specified here), the method should check the board state after the last move.

Since the exact winning condition is not explicitly given, a common approach is:

- If the last move captured a piece that is a "King" or a special piece, return lastPlayer as winner.
- Or if the opponent has no pieces left on the board, lastPlayer wins.
- Otherwise, return null.

Here is a simple implementation assuming the winning condition is that the opponent has no pieces left on the board after the last move:

```java
@Override
public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
    // Check if opponent has any pieces left on the board
    Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
    for (Player player : players) {
        if (!player.equals(lastPlayer)) {
            boolean opponentHasPieces = false;
            for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
                for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
                    Piece piece = board[x][y];
                    if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                        opponentHasPieces = true;
                        break;
                    }
                }
                if (opponentHasPieces) break;
            }
            if (!opponentHasPieces) {
                return lastPlayer; // lastPlayer wins because opponent has no pieces left
            }
        }
    }
    // No winner yet
    return null;
}
```

This method iterates over all players except the lastPlayer, checks if they have any pieces left on the board, and if none found, declares lastPlayer as winner. Otherwise, returns null. Adjust the logic if your game has a different winning condition.

Response Text:---
The method `updateScore` should calculate the Manhattan distance between the source and destination places of the move, then add this distance to the player's current score.

The Manhattan distance between two points `(x1, y1)` and `(x2, y2)` is `|x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|`.

Here is a complete implementation of the `updateScore` method:

```java
public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();
    int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
    int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
    player.setScore(newScore);
}
```

Response Text:---
The method `getAvailableMoves` should collect all valid moves of all pieces owned by the given player. It iterates over the board, finds pieces owned by the player, calls each piece's `getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)` method, and accumulates these moves into a list. Finally, it returns all collected moves as an array.

Here is a correct implementation of the method:

```java
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place place = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] pieceMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, place);
                if (pieceMoves != null) {
                    moves.addAll(Arrays.asList(pieceMoves));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

This ensures all moves returned belong to the player's pieces and are gathered from each piece's own logic.

The `validate` method should check whether both the source and destination positions of the move are within the boundaries of the game board. Typically, the `Game` interface provides access to the board dimensions or a method to check if a position is valid. Assuming `Game` has methods like `getBoardWidth()`, `getBoardHeight()`, and `isInsideBoard(Position pos)` or at least width and height, you can implement the boundary check accordingly.

Here is a complete implementation of the `validate` method that returns `true` only if both source and destination positions are inside the board boundaries:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    int width = game.getBoardWidth();
    int height = game.getBoardHeight();

    int srcX = move.getSource().getX();
    int srcY = move.getSource().getY();
    int destX = move.getDestination().getX();
    int destY = move.getDestination().getY();

    boolean sourceInside = srcX >= 0 && srcX < width && srcY >= 0 && srcY < height;
    boolean destinationInside = destX >= 0 && destX < width && destY >= 0 && destY < height;

    return sourceInside && destinationInside;
}
```

The method `getAvailableMoves` should generate all possible knight moves from the current position, then filter out invalid moves using the provided `validateMove` method. A knight moves in an "L" shape: two squares in one direction and one square perpendicular. We consider all 8 possible moves, create `Move` objects with the source and each candidate destination, validate them, and collect the valid ones.

Here is a complete implementation of the method:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    int[][] knightMoves = {
        {2, 1}, {2, -1}, {-2, 1}, {-2, -1},
        {1, 2}, {1, -2}, {-1, 2}, {-1, -2}
    };
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    int sourceRow = source.getRow();
    int sourceCol = source.getColumn();

    for (int[] moveOffset : knightMoves) {
        int destRow = sourceRow + moveOffset[0];
        int destCol = sourceCol + moveOffset[1];
        Place destination = new Place(destRow, destCol);
        Move move = new Move(source, destination);
        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
            validMoves.add(move);
        }
    }

    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new KnightMoveRule(),
				new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}
}

Response Text:---
The `getAvailableMoves` method for the `Archer` piece should generate all possible moves according to the Archer's movement rules (similar to the cannon in Xiangqi). The Archer moves orthogonally any number of empty squares, but to capture, it must jump exactly one piece (the "screen") before landing on an opponent piece.

The method should:
- Iterate in all four orthogonal directions (up, down, left, right).
- For each direction, move step by step:
  - First, move through empty squares and add those as valid moves.
  - Then, if a piece is encountered (the screen), continue beyond it:
    - The next piece encountered after the screen can be captured (valid move).
    - No further moves beyond that.
- Use `validateMove` to ensure the move is valid according to all rules.

Here is a complete implementation of `getAvailableMoves`:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    int srcRow = source.getRow();
    int srcCol = source.getColumn();

    // Directions: up, down, left, right
    int[][] directions = { {-1, 0}, {1, 0}, {0, -1}, {0, 1} };

    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int dRow = dir[0];
        int dCol = dir[1];
        boolean screenFound = false;

        int r = srcRow + dRow;
        int c = srcCol + dCol;

        while (game.getConfiguration().isValidPlace(r, c)) {
            Place target = new Place(r, c);
            var pieceAtTarget = game.getPieceAt(target);

            if (!screenFound) {
                if (pieceAtTarget == null) {
                    // Empty square before screen: valid move
                    Move move = new Move(source, target);
                    if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                        moves.add(move);
                    }
                    r += dRow;
                    c += dCol;
                } else {
                    // Found the screen piece
                    screenFound = true;
                    r += dRow;
                    c += dCol;
                }
            } else {
                // After screen found, next piece can be captured if opponent's piece
                if (pieceAtTarget != null) {
                    // Capture move
                    Move move = new Move(source, target);
                    if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                        moves.add(move);
                    }
                    break; // no moves beyond capture
                } else {
                    // Empty square beyond screen: cannot move here
                    r += dRow;
                    c += dCol;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(Move[]::new);
}
```

This implementation respects the Archer's movement rules and uses the provided `validateMove` method to ensure all moves are legal.

				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(), };

Response Text:---
The `validate` method should check if the move of an Archer piece is valid according to its special moving rule, similar to the cannon in Xiangqi. Typically, an Archer moves like a rook but must jump exactly one piece when capturing, and cannot jump when moving without capturing.

A correct implementation will:
- Check if the move is strictly horizontal or vertical.
- Count the number of pieces between source and destination.
- If the destination is empty, no pieces should be in between.
- If the destination has an opponent piece, exactly one piece should be in between.

Here is a complete implementation of the `validate` method for `ArcherMoveRule`:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    var source = move.getSource();
    var destination = move.getDestination();

    int srcRow = source.row();
    int srcCol = source.col();
    int destRow = destination.row();
    int destCol = destination.col();

    // Archer moves only in straight lines (horizontal or vertical)
    if (srcRow != destRow && srcCol != destCol) {
        return false;
    }

    int countBetween = 0;

    if (srcRow == destRow) {
        // Horizontal move
        int start = Math.min(srcCol, destCol) + 1;
        int end = Math.max(srcCol, destCol);
        for (int c = start; c < end; c++) {
            if (game.getPiece(new assignment.protocol.Position(srcRow, c)) != null) {
                countBetween++;
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Vertical move
        int start = Math.min(srcRow, destRow) + 1;
        int end = Math.max(srcRow, destRow);
        for (int r = start; r < end; r++) {
            if (game.getPiece(new assignment.protocol.Position(r, srcCol)) != null) {
                countBetween++;
            }
        }
    }

    var destPiece = game.getPiece(destination);

    if (destPiece == null) {
        // Moving without capturing: no pieces between source and destination
        return countBetween == 0;
    } else {
        // Capturing: exactly one piece between source and destination
        // Also, cannot capture own piece
        var srcPiece = game.getPiece(source);
        if (srcPiece.getOwner().equals(destPiece.getOwner())) {
            return false;
        }
        return countBetween == 1;
    }
}

@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    var source = move.getSource();
    var destination = move.getDestination();

    int srcRow = source.row();
    int srcCol = source.col();
    int destRow = destination.row();
    int destCol = destination.col();

    // Archer moves only in straight lines (horizontal or vertical)
    if (srcRow != destRow && srcCol != destCol) {
        return false;

    int countBetween = 0;

        // Horizontal move

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    var source = move.getSource();
    var destination = move.getDestination();

    int srcRow = source.getRow();
    int srcCol = source.getCol();
    int destRow = destination.getRow();
    int destCol = destination.getCol();

    // Archer moves only in straight lines (horizontal or vertical)
    if (srcRow != destRow && srcCol != destCol) {
        return false;
    }

    int countBetween = 0;

    if (srcRow == destRow) {
        // Horizontal move
        int start = Math.min(srcCol, destCol) + 1;
        int end = Math.max(srcCol, destCol);
        for (int c = start; c < end; c++) {
            if (game.getPiece(new assignment.protocol.Place(srcRow, c)) != null) {
                countBetween++;
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Vertical move
        int start = Math.min(srcRow, destRow) + 1;
        int end = Math.max(srcRow, destRow);
        for (int r = start; r < end; r++) {
            if (game.getPiece(new assignment.protocol.Place(r, srcCol)) != null) {
                countBetween++;
            }
        }
    }

    var destPiece = game.getPiece(destination);

    if (destPiece == null) {
        // Moving without capturing: no pieces between source and destination
        return countBetween == 0;
    } else {
        // Capturing: exactly one piece between source and destination
        // Also, cannot capture own piece
        var srcPiece = game.getPiece(source);
        if (srcPiece.getPlayer().equals(destPiece.getPlayer())) {
            return false;
        }
        return countBetween == 1;
    }
}

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    assignment.protocol.Place source = move.getSource();
    assignment.protocol.Place destination = move.getDestination();

    int srcRow = source.row();
    int srcCol = source.col();
    int destRow = destination.row();
    int destCol = destination.col();

    // Archer moves only in straight lines (horizontal or vertical)
    if (srcRow != destRow && srcCol != destCol) {
        return false;
    }

    int countBetween = 0;

    if (srcRow == destRow) {
        // Horizontal move
        int start = Math.min(srcCol, destCol) + 1;
        int end = Math.max(srcCol, destCol);
        for (int c = start; c < end; c++) {
            if (game.getPiece(new assignment.protocol.Place(srcRow, c)) != null) {
                countBetween++;
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Vertical move
        int start = Math.min(srcRow, destRow) + 1;
        int end = Math.max(srcRow, destRow);
        for (int r = start; r < end; r++) {
            if (game.getPiece(new assignment.protocol.Place(r, srcCol)) != null) {
                countBetween++;
            }
        }
    }

    var destPiece = game.getPiece(destination);

    if (destPiece == null) {
        // Moving without capturing: no pieces between source and destination
        return countBetween == 0;
    } else {
        // Capturing: exactly one piece between source and destination
        // Also, cannot capture own piece
        var srcPiece = game.getPiece(source);
        if (srcPiece.getPlayer().equals(destPiece.getPlayer())) {
            return false;
        }
        return countBetween == 1;
    }
}

The `validate` method should check if the move made by a Knight piece is valid according to chess rules. A Knight moves in an "L" shape: two squares in one direction (horizontal or vertical) and then one square perpendicular to that. The method should calculate the difference in row and column between the source and destination squares and verify this pattern.

Here is a complete implementation of the `validate` method for the `KnightMoveRule` class:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }
    int srcRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int srcCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int destRow = move.getDestination().getRow();
    int destCol = move.getDestination().getCol();

    int rowDiff = Math.abs(destRow - srcRow);
    int colDiff = Math.abs(destCol - srcCol);

    // Knight moves in L shape: (2,1) or (1,2)
    return (rowDiff == 2 && colDiff == 1) || (rowDiff == 1 && colDiff == 2);
}
```

This method returns `true` if the move is a valid Knight move, otherwise `false`.

Response Text:---
The `validate` method should check if the knight's move is blocked in a way similar to the "horse leg" rule in Xiangqi (Chinese chess). In Xiangqi, a knight moves one step orthogonally and then one step diagonally outward. The move is blocked if the orthogonal step is occupied by any piece.

To implement this, you need to:
1. Determine the source and destination coordinates.
2. Calculate the orthogonal step (the "leg") that must be free for the knight to move.
3. Check if the "leg" position is occupied.
4. Return `false` if blocked, otherwise `true`.

Here is a complete implementation of the `validate` method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }

    Place source = move.getSource();
    Place destination = move.getDestination();

    int dx = destination.getX() - source.getX();
    int dy = destination.getY() - source.getY();

    // Knight moves in an "L" shape: 2 by 1 or 1 by 2
    // Identify the "leg" position that must be free
    Place leg;

    if (Math.abs(dx) == 2 && Math.abs(dy) == 1) {
        // Horizontal move first, then vertical
        leg = new Place(source.getX() + dx / 2, source.getY());
    } else if (Math.abs(dx) == 1 && Math.abs(dy) == 2) {
        // Vertical move first, then horizontal
        leg = new Place(source.getX(), source.getY() + dy / 2);
    } else {
        // Not a valid knight move shape, let other rules handle this
        return true;
    }

    // If the "leg" position is occupied, the knight is blocked
    return game.getPiece(leg) == null;
}
```

This method returns `true` if the knight is not blocked and the move shape is valid, otherwise `false`.

Response Text:---
The `validate` method should check if the destination position of the `move` is already occupied by a piece belonging to the same player who is making the move. If so, the move is invalid and the method returns `false`; otherwise, it returns `true`.

Here is a complete implementation of the `validate` method for the `OccupiedRule` class:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    var destination = move.getDestination();
    var pieceAtDestination = game.getPieceAt(destination);
    if (pieceAtDestination == null) {
        return true; // no piece at destination, move is valid
    }
    var movingPiece = game.getPieceAt(move.getOrigin());
    if (movingPiece == null) {
        return false; // no piece to move, invalid move
    }
    // move is invalid if the piece at destination belongs to the same player
    return !movingPiece.getPlayer().equals(pieceAtDestination.getPlayer());
}
```

This assumes that `Game` has methods `getPieceAt(Position)` and that `Piece` has a `getPlayer()` method to identify the owner.

public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {

    while (true) {

                break;
            }

            System.out.println("Move not in available moves. Please try again.");
            continue;
        }
        String validationError = validateMove(game, move);

            System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationError);

	 * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
	 * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.

	 * facilitate programming.
	 * This is VERY different from the coordinate used in console display.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param game           the current game object
	 * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
	 * @return the chosen move
	 */

	public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
		// TODO student implementation
